pageCache.pageTitle: Music - Stepney Greencoat C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Music
With over 40 languages spoken at our school, at Stepney Greencoat we believe that one thing every culture has in common is music. Music is a world-wide language that allows expression, creativity, celebration, a means of escape, praising and worshiping God, reflection, and storytelling.
Our aim is that by the time our pupils leave our school, they will have developed the key skills needed to continually progress and develop their musicianship in singing, listening, composing, learning an instrument, improvising, and performing.
At Stepney Greencoat, we also work collaboratively with THAMES (Tower Hamlets Advisory Music and Education Service) music group to offer pupils the opportunity to receive discrete music lessons. This currently includes lessons in African drumming, the recorder and brass instruments.
In 2021, we were awarded the Music Mark Certificate in recognition of high-quality music education for all children and young people.
Across the years, pupils at Stepney Greencoat will:
Listen to, perform, review, and evaluate music
Music – “Learning Together for Life”
Learning
Our pupils will have the opportunity to learn through music and about music, starting with movement, feelings, and rhythm in Reception to theory, notation, improvisation, and composition in Year 6. Our pupils will engage in the history of songs and musicians - understanding the story behind the songs that we sing and the message that can be brought to the world through music.
Together
We are made up of incredibly unique individuals, with incredibly unique skill sets and we celebrate our differences, by partnering with our musical experts to deliver and bring our pupils a taste of music from different cultures and periods of time. Joining in concerts with our local schools, provides our pupils with a sense of belonging and community.
Life
Through music, we aim to provide our children with rich experiences in life through with opportunities such as live performances, visits, and workshops by the London Symphony Orchestra and the London Philharmonic Orchestra.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art - Stepney Greencoat C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Art
At Stepney Greencoat, we believe that Art stimulates creativity and imagination - enabling children to communicate what they see, feel and think through the elements of line, shape, colour, form, texture and space.
Our opportunities provide visual, tactile and sensory experiences, and give children a special way of understanding and responding to the world.
We have adopted the Access Art scheme of work that consists of 36 pathways for Years 1 to 6, designed to inspire and enable high quality visual arts teaching and learning.
The scheme is designed around the idea that art is far more than a series of technical skills, and this holistic curriculum nurtures creative thinking skills and helps ensure your pupils learn through art, as well as about art.

pageCache.text:
Computing
At Stepney Greencoat, we recognise that the rapid development of technology in the home, the workplace and the wider community has had, and will continue to have, an immense impact on the lives of our pupils.
We value the use of Computing as a teaching and learning tool for both children and adults and we seek to encourage pupils to become autonomous and independent in its use.
At Stepney Greencoat, we follow the National Centre for Computing Education primary scheme of work which meets the requirements of the National curriculum through practical, creative, and knowledge-rich lessons that include computer science, digital literacy, programming as well as digital safety.

pageCache.pageTitle: Early Years - Stepney Greencoat C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Early Years
At Stepney Greencoat our EYFS comprises of one Reception class and one Nursery class that each follow the curriculum as outlined in the latest version of the EYFS statutory framework.
It is every child’s right to grow up safe, healthy, enjoying and achieving, making a positive contribution and with economic well-being.
The EYFS principles which guide the work of all practitioners are grouped into four distinct but complementary themes:
Learning and Development
The Early learning goals (the knowledge, skills and understanding which young children should acquire by the end of the reception year) and the educational programmes (the matters, skills and processes which are required to be taught to young children) are set out in the “Statutory Framework for the Early Years Foundation Stage” document.
There seven areas of learning and development:
Prime
Communication & Language and Literacy (C&L)
Physical Development (PD)
Personal, Social and Emotional Development (PSED)
Specific
At Stepney Greencoat we believe these seven areas are equally important and depend on each other to support a rounded approach to child development. We aim to deliver all the areas through planned, purposeful play, with a balance of adult-led and child-initiated activities.
Literacy
Mathematics
Understanding the World (UW)
Expressive arts and design (EAD)
Learning through play
“Play is essential for children’s development, building their confidence as they learn to explore, to think about problems, and relate to others.”
(“Early Years Foundation Stage”, 2014)
At Stepney Greencoat, we support children’s learning through planned play activities, and decide when child-initiated or adult-led play activities would provide the most effective learning opportunities. We believe that it is important for adults to support children’s learning through play, by getting involved in the play themselves and through sustained shared thinking.
Home/School Links
We recognise that parents/guardians are the child’s first and most enduring educators. When parents/guardians and practitioners work together in Early Years settings, the results have a positive impact on the child’s development. A successful partnership needs to be a two-way flow of information, knowledge and expertise.
We aim to develop this by:
• outlining the Nursery /Reception curriculum to parents/guardians during the new parents meeting in July, to enable them to understand the value of supporting their child’s learning at home.
• sending home letters, informing parents/guardians of the learning that will be taking place at school.
• holding parent/carer evenings to discuss progress and to provide an opportunity for asking questions and sharing information.
• operating an “open door” policy, whereby parents/guardians can come and discuss concerns and developments in an informal manner.
• inviting parents/guardians to help in our school and to accompany children on school visits.
• encouraging parents/guardians to listen to their child read each night and to comment on reading progress in a home/school reading diary.
• providing an annual written report to parents/guardians in July summarising the child’s progress against the early learning goals and their characteristics of learning.

History
At Stepney Greencoat, our History curriculum is designed to inspire pupils’ curiosity to know more about the past. The curriculum is tailored to meet the needs of our children and explore the rich background, history, culture and diversity of the City we live in.
We aim to give our pupils learning experiences that teach them to make meaningful links between their own lives and those of people from the past. The curriculum also includes several local historical links with London and the East End.
Many of our Literacy units also have an historical theme allowing pupils to broaden their understanding further outside of our history lessons.

pageCache.text:
Maths
At Stepney Greencoat, we teach Mathematics that helps children to make sense of the world around them through developing their ability to calculate, reason and solve problems. We do this through the adoption of the White Rose Maths schemes of work.
The White Rose Maths curriculum recognises that a good understanding of basic mathematics is essential wherever calculations, measurements, graphical interpretations and statistical analyses are necessary.
The program is designed to instil a deeper understanding of mathematical concepts using a full range of fun, inspiring classroom activities to develop confident and inquisitive mathematicians.

pageCache.pageTitle: Modern Foreign Languages - Stepney Greencoat C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages
At Stepney Greencoat, we believe that language learning is an important element in our ability to make connections with other people, develop friendships, explore cultures and become active global citizens. Here at Stepney Greencoat, our Key Stage Two pupils have weekly French lessons involving a wide range of activities including songs, stories, games and role-play.
Our teachers follow the Rachel Hawkes - French scheme of work - which "draws on key recommendations from the pedagogy review and the Ofsted languages research report, highlighting the three key knowledge strands: phonics, vocabulary, and grammar. They also exploit everyday and rich cultural contexts to build confident communication in the new language."

pageCache.pageTitle: Religious Education - Stepney Greencoat C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Religious Education
At Stepney Greencoat, our RE curriculum is taught weekly and we follow the London Diocese Board for Schools scheme of work which covers both Christianity and other major religions. This gives our pupils the opportunity to understand people’s beliefs, compare them with their own and learn to respect each other’s views and faith.
We recognise and value the sacredness of each individual in our community and aim to deliver our school Vision through the teaching of Religious Education, Collective Worship, building relationships and celebrating the Christian traditions within our school and parish community.
We understand that quality RE learning can only be achieved in an environment where everyone perceives themselves to be valued, loved and are learning to value each other - which underpins all that we do at Stepney Greencoat.
If you have any questions about our RE curriculum at Stepney Greencoat, please get in touch via office2@stepneygreencoat.towerhamlets.sch.uk - with the subject 'RE Questions'
Parents who wish to exercise their right to withdraw their child from Religious Education or Collective Worship will need to contact the Headteacher to discuss arrangements for alternative provision.

Science
At Stepney Greencoat, we believe that children have both a natural curiosity about their world and a boundless enthusiasm to make sense of it. With this in mind, we aim to harness both their curiosity and enthusiasm to enable our children to acquire the knowledge, skills and attitudes needed to prepare them for life in the increasingly scientific and technological age that they live in.
Here at Stepney Greencoat, we know that the teaching of Science develops interest in the world around them and fosters a respect for the environment so by providing children with first-hand experiences, our pupils come face to face with phenomena and learn directly about the way things are and why they behave as they do.
We aim to teach the Science curriculum in subject specific lessons that revisit key concepts and build on previous learning.

Appeals
If your child is not offered a place at a school of your preference, you may appeal against that decision. The appeal panel is independent of the council and the school.
If you wish to appeal you must complete and submit the school’s Admission Appeals form which will be sent to you with the letter informing you that you have not been offered a place. You can also download the form from our website (see below), or ask the school office for a copy.
The Admission Appeal form should be sent to the Clerk to the Appeals panel at the school address. Please include any evidence or supporting material with your appeal and you must give the reasons for your appeal at the time the appeal is submitted.

pageCache.pageTitle: Vision and Values - Stepney Greencoat C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our Vision: Learning Together for Life
Jesus said, ‘Love one another as I have loved you’ - John 15:12, New Testament.
Our vision and associated values are rooted in God’s word the Holy Bible. For all members of our school community to be loving towards each other as Jesus loves us is central to all that we do, enabling us to learn effectively, work harmoniously and live well in God’s world.​
Values
'And let us run with perseverance the race marked out for us' - Hebrews 12:1
'Love your neighbour as yourself' - Matthew 22:36
'Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free' - John 8:32
'Show proper respect to everyone, love the family of believers, fear God' - 1 Peter 2:17a
'there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother' - Proverbs 18:24b
'But I trust in your unfailing love; my heart rejoices in your salvation' - Psalm 13:5
God's Word the Bible is the core of our values
'All scripture is breathed out by God' - 2 Timothy 3.16
The core of our values is God’s Word the Bible. This is because, scripture is at the heart of the teaching, learning, understanding and application of our vision and our values.
We strive to provide our children with a sound knowledge of the Bible as a collection of books, both in the Old and New Testaments and of the stories within these books.
